title: Sass with Modern CSS Functions knowledge check

questions.prompt: Which mental model best explains “Sass with Modern CSS Functions” in Dart Sass?
options: Readable SCSS guarantees correct browser rendering, accessibility, and performance without output review.
The best solution is always to replace native CSS behavior with a new Sass abstraction.

Dart Sass groups built-ins into namespaced modules such as `sass:math`, `sass:color`, `sass:list`, `sass:map`, `sass:string`, `sass:meta`, and `sass:selector`. Load the module you need and read its argument and return-value contract.
The browser executes Sass source directly, so a compilation step is unnecessary.
questions.answer_key: Dart Sass groups built-ins into namespaced modules such as `sass:math`, `sass:color`, `sass:list`, `sass:map`, `sass:string`, `sass:meta`, and `sass:selector`. Load the module you need and read its argument and return-value contract.
questions.explanation: Dart Sass groups built-ins into namespaced modules such as `sass:math`, `sass:color`, `sass:list`, `sass:map`, `sass:string`, `sass:meta`, and `sass:selector`. Load the module you need and read its argument and return-value contract. The alternative choices confuse Sass compilation with browser execution or claim guarantees that require independent tests.

questions.prompt: When applying “calc() and related calculations”, which approach is the most reliable?
options: Silence every warning before determining whether it identifies a deprecated or incorrect construct.
Check the type and unit of each operand and decide whether the calculation belongs in Sass at build time or in CSS at browser runtime.
Skip compilation and infer the final selector list and property values from the source file alone.
Prefer deeply nested selectors because fewer source lines always mean simpler and safer CSS.
questions.answer_key: Check the type and unit of each operand and decide whether the calculation belongs in Sass at build time or in CSS at browser runtime.
questions.explanation: Check the type and unit of each operand and decide whether the calculation belongs in Sass at build time or in CSS at browser runtime. Compare the compiled output with the stated intent and preserve browser-native behavior where it is required.

questions.prompt: Which review decision most directly supports maintainability for “Sass with Modern CSS Functions”?
options: Keep compiler-time calculations separate from CSS functions that should run in the browser. Test missing keys, invalid indices, unit compatibility, and color-space assumptions instead of hiding errors behind a fallback.
Generate every possible selector or theme combination, even when most variants are never used.
Treat successful compilation as proof that the interface is accessible and behaves correctly in every browser.
Expose internal implementation details as public API and postpone documentation until after release.
questions.answer_key: Keep compiler-time calculations separate from CSS functions that should run in the browser. Test missing keys, invalid indices, unit compatibility, and color-space assumptions instead of hiding errors behind a fallback.
questions.explanation: Keep compiler-time calculations separate from CSS functions that should run in the browser. Test missing keys, invalid indices, unit compatibility, and color-space assumptions instead of hiding errors behind a fallback. The other choices increase output, assume unverified behavior, or make the public interface harder to maintain.
